h: The Wine of Kiddush Repairs the Root of Forgetfulness

p: At the third meal of Shabbos
our Sages, of blessed memory, did not institute
Now the Kiddush of Shabbos night,
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said:
means to say the sanctification of the day,
is fit to make Kiddush over
all the songs and praises in the world."
which is only a blessing of enjoyment,
For the remembrance at its entry
is that he should remember that it is Shabbos,
and by Torah law it suffices
when one sanctifies it at its entry;
a place that has no forgetting,
and forgetting does not exist in it
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב צב, ב)
when the yetzer hara returned to its place,
one needs guarding all of Shabbos
the whole business of the yetzer hara,
"And it shall be, if you forget,"
הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ פֶּן תִּשְׁכַּח וְגוֹ׳ (שָׁם ח, יא)
at the time of the yetzer hara
our Sages, of blessed memory, instituted:
so that through this he will remember
And the matter is based on
מַה שֶּׁאָמַר בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא בַתְרָא נח, ב)
And it is based on the Pesikta
with the thing with which I strike,
A man strikes with a scalpel
'For I will bring healing to you,
and from your wounds I will heal you.'"
is because of the corruption of the serpent;
for were it not for the corruption
no healing would have been needed,
"And He will heal the wound of His blow"
He will heal the wound of the blow of the world.
"'And Hashem will remove from you all illness'
this is the yetzer hara, etc.";
is the cause of all illnesses,
there would have been no illness at all.
And regarding the corruption of the serpent,
And although there is a dispute about this
it says in the Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 24):
and all of it is true"
And since the root of the corruption
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּאוּ כָּל הַחוֹלָאִים
and through this came all the illnesses,
"And from your wounds I will heal you";
and this is what it says:
"At the head of all medicines am I, wine."
through wine there will be benefit,
that he will remember to keep Shabbos.
they instituted saying Kiddush with the mouth
and in the morning it suffices
to drink the wine of a mitzvah,
he will remember to keep Shabbos.
at the night meal and in the morning;
which is at the end of Shabbos,
when he has already merited to keep it all day
and although there is still time
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כֵּיוָן שֶׁזָּכַר כָּל הַיּוֹם
nevertheless, since he remembered all day
he will surely remember this hour too
at this meal they did not further institute
